item.title: Hardening from the Ground Up: Using Distroless Base Images
item.description: You just wired Trivy into your pipeline. First real scan, on a Node.js API that does nothing more exotic than call three internal REST endpoints and write to Postgres. The output comes back: 43 CVEs. You brace for the worst and start reading through them, and here’s the thing — your package.json has eleven dependencies, and none of them show up in the list. Every single finding traces back to bash, tar, perl, openssl-libs, and a dozen other packages that shipped with node:18 because that’s what full OS base images do. Your application never imports any of them. It never will. But Trivy doesn’t know that, and neither does the attacker who lands a shell in your container — they’ll happily use curl to pull a second-stage payload, because you handed it to them for free.
